properties.snippet: Travel around Tennessee and learn about the field monitoring efforts by the Tennessee Wildlife Resources Agency's Biodiversity Staff
properties.description: This study examines pathogen prevalence in Eastern Box Turtles (EBTs) within Tennessee’s Central Basin, where habitat fragmentation, loss, and urbanization create major ecological pressures. These stressors, combined with limited green space, may heighten pathogen susceptibility and alter EBT behavior. We hypothesize that turtles in fragmented habitats exhibit higher co-pathogen detection rates due to restricted movement and reduced habitat connectivity. Turtles were notched, swabbed, and fitted with radio transmitters at Ellington Agricultural Center and the Nashville Zoo. Weather, habitat, and behavioral data were systematically collected during field surveys at each detection site. We expect findings to reveal increased co-pathogen prevalence and notable behavioral or movement changes in infected individuals, providing insights into EBT disease ecology and informing habitat management strategies in the Central Basin.

properties.snippet: Official boundaries for all State Forests managed by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). This is the authoritative dataset for TDF-managed forest lands.
properties.description:
Tennessee State Forest Boundaries

Overview

This feature layer represents the official and authoritative boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry (TDF). The polygons in this dataset delineate the properties managed by the TDF for sustainable forestry, wildlife habitat, soil and water conservation, and public recreation.

This dataset is intended for use in planning, management, analysis, and public information purposes. It serves as the primary GIS data source for all TDF-managed forest properties.

Feature Layer

  • Tennessee State Forest Boundaries: This polygon layer represents the official boundaries of all State Forests administered by the Tennessee Division of Forestry. 

Data Attributes

  • StateForestName: The common name of the State Forest.
  • AbbrCode: The abbreviated codes.
  • County: The county(ies) that the State Forest is located in.
  • District: The TDF Administrative District that the State Forest is located in.
  • Acres: The calculated acreage of the property.
  • Latitude: Latitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • Longitude: Longitude of the center point of the property, in Decimal Degrees.
  • YearEst: The year that the State Forest was established.
  • Notes: Additional notes.
  • CollectionMethod: The method of boundary delineation.
  • Hyperlink: The hyperlink to the State Forests' webpage.

Data Maintenance

This layer is actively maintained by the TDF Forest Data and Analysis Unit. It is updated periodically to reflect new acquisitions, boundary surveys, and other administrative changes.

properties.description:
InFORM FODR

This dataset represents Fire Occurrence Data Record (FODR) incidents produced by the Interagency Fire Occurrence Reporting Modules (InFORM) Application and displayed for the State of Tennessee. The FODR is the authoritative fire occurrence dataset for the five major federal fire management agencies and some state agencies. It also includes records bulk uploaded by state agencies that do not participate directly in InFORM, supporting a comprehensive national fire occurrence dataset.

This dataset is part of an ongoing project to consolidate interagency fire point data. The incorporation of all available historical data is in progress.

The InFORM FODR records are the official record of fire events. Built on top of IRWIN, the Integrated Reporting of Wildland Fire Information system, the FODR starts with an IRWIN record and then captures the final incident information upon certification of the record by the appropriate local authority.

This Tennessee-focused visualization is filtered from the source InFORM FODR incident service to display wildland fire incidents located within Tennessee that meet the following criteria:

  • Categorized as a Wildfire (WF) or Prescribed Fire (RX) record
  • Valid and not “quarantined” due to potential conflicts with other records
  • No “fall-off” rules are applied to this service
  • Displayed from a real-time source service

This dataset is intended to support wildfire planning, situational awareness, fire occurrence analysis, interagency coordination, and public information purposes within Tennessee.

Warning: Users should refrain from repeatedly querying the source service using a relative date range. This includes using the “in the last” or “not in the last” operators in a web map filter or any reference to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. This type of query puts undue load on the source service and may render it temporarily unavailable.

properties.snippet: Detailed GIS data depicting state-owned lands in Tennessee including point locations and boundaries (estimated, GIS parcel, and survey) with jurisdiction and property management details. This data does not include easements. It does including a growing number of leases and right-of-way objects. Please report any errors in the data to chuck.j.sutherland@tn.gov.
properties.description:
Overview

This Feature Service provides detailed geographic information on state-owned lands within Tennessee. It represents parcels of land managed by various departments and divisions of the Tennessee state government.

Feature Layers

  • StateOwnedLands Points: This layer contains point locations of state-owned land parcels, including key attributes such as property name, managing jurisdiction, and legislative district information. The points also provide latitude and longitude coordinates which represent parcel centroids.
  • StateOwnedLands Polygons: This polygon layer depicts the spatial extent of state-owned land parcels, allowing for analysis of property boundaries and calculated land areas. Attributes include property names, jurisdictional management, stream protection status, and legislative district names.

Attribution

  • Property ID: Unique identifier for each record.
  • GISLINK: An ID to match records to specific parcels. 
  • property_name: Should match the language used by the organization that manages the property.
  • dv_id_juris: The department of Tennessee government that manages the property.
  • stream_status: Determined by the team that manages the property. Higher education property is not assessed by STREAM.
  • Legal Interest: Owned or Leased
  • County_Name: The county the center of the property falls within.
  • House Name: The representative whose district the center of the property falls within.
  • Senate Name: The senator whose district the center of the property falls within.

Geographic Coverage

The dataset exclusively covers the state of Tennessee, incorporating parcel data sourced from county tax assessors and internal state databases. It excludes easements, but contains a growing number of leases and rights-of-way objects.

Purpose and Use Cases

  • This data supports asset management and planning for Tennessee state land holdings.
  • It is useful for environmental management, policy making, and legislative referencing for state properties.
  • The layers can be applied in mapping projects, public information systems, and spatial analyses related to state land use and jurisdiction.

Credit
Department of General Services, State of Tennessee Real Estate Asset Management, Portfolio and Performance Analytics

properties.description:
Wildland Fire Incident Locations

This dataset represents Wildland Fire Incident Locations displayed for the State of Tennessee. The data consists of operational fire occurrence records reported to IRWIN, the Integrated Reporting of Wildland Fire Information system, and reflects a snapshot in time of what was known for each incident during the operational period of the fire.

This dataset is preserved as operational incident information. It is not QA/QC’d after a fire is declared out and may differ from the authoritative InFORM Fire Occurrence Data Record locations.

The Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (WFIGS) Group provides authoritative geospatial data products under the interagency Wildland Fire Data Program. Hosted in the National Interagency Fire Center ArcGIS Online Organization, WFIGS provides both internal and public-facing data in a variety of formats.

This Tennessee-focused visualization is filtered from the source IRWIN incident service to display wildland fire incidents located within Tennessee that meet the following criteria:

  • Categorized as a Wildfire (WF), Prescribed Fire (RX), or Incident Complex (CX) record
  • Valid and not “quarantined” in IRWIN due to potential conflicts with other records
  • No “fall-off” rules are applied to this service
  • Records extend from present day back to 2014, when IRWIN was implemented
  • Data are refreshed from the IRWIN source every 5 minutes

The criteria for inclusion were determined by a National Wildfire Coordinating Group (NWCG) Geospatial Subcommittee task group.

This dataset is intended to support operational situational awareness, wildfire planning, incident review, interagency coordination, analysis, and public information purposes within Tennessee.

Warning: Users should refrain from repeatedly querying the source service using a relative date range. This includes using the “in the last” or “not in the last” operators in a web map filter or any reference to CURRENT_TIMESTAMP. This type of query puts undue load on the source service and may render it temporarily unavailable.
properties.licenseInfo:
This dataset is provided as a Tennessee-focused visualization of Wildland Fire Incident Locations from the IRWIN incident service. The source data is hosted and maintained by the Wildland Fire Interagency Geospatial Services (WFIGS) Group under the interagency Wildland Fire Data Program.

The Tennessee Division of Forestry does not own, modify, or independently maintain the source IRWIN data represented in this service. Records are operational in nature and represent a snapshot in time of what was known during the operational period of each incident.

This dataset is intended for operational situational awareness, wildfire planning, incident review, interagency coordination, analysis, and public information purposes. It should not be used as the sole source for emergency response, legal determinations, enforcement actions, official incident documentation, or final fire occurrence reporting.

Incident records may change as additional information becomes available. This data is not QA/QC’d after a fire is declared out and may differ from the authoritative InFORM Fire Occurrence Data Record locations.

The information is provided “as is” without warranty or guarantee of any kind as to its accuracy, content, completeness, timeliness, legality, or reliability. Use of this dataset is subject to any applicable terms, conditions, limitations, or restrictions established by the source data provider and hosting service.

properties.snippet: This NDVI imagery layer features recent high-resolution (1m or better) aerial imagery for the continental United States, made available by the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center.
properties.description:
This Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) layer features recent high-resolution (1-meter or better) aerial imagery for the continental United States, made available by the USDA Farm Production and Conservation Business Center (FPAC). The National Agriculture Imagery Program (NAIP) acquires aerial imagery during the agricultural growing seasons in the continental United States. Approximately half of the US is collected each year and each state is typically collected every other year.

This imagery layer is updated annually as new imagery is made available. The NAIP program aims to make the imagery available to governmental agencies and to the public within a year of collection. The imagery is published in 4-bands (Red, Green, Blue, and Near Infrared) where available. Additional NAIP renderings include Natural Color and Color Infrared.

 

Key Properties

Geographic Coverage: Continental United States (Hawaii and Puerto Rico available for some years)
Temporal Coverage: 2010 to 2023
Spatial Resolution: 0.3-meter to 1-meter
Revisit Time: Typically every other year
Source Data Coordinate System: Universal Transverse Mercator (UTM) WGS84
Service Coordinate System: Web Mercator Auxiliary Sphere WGS84 (EPSG:3857)
Analysis: Optimized for analysis
